D1_support: 55-question bank developed from a 108-question pool using web-based retrieval, Google Trends, PubMed-informed topic review, patient education resources and expert screening (Abstract/Methods as preserved); screening criteria and item disposition are not in the preserved full text, so sampling reproducibility is No information.
D2_support: Six models with per-model query dates 12-19 May 2026 reported verbatim; prompt handling (new session, single submission, temperature/browsing/system settings) and prompt-set availability are not reported in the preserved full text. The second round was post hoc and analysed only as a matched retest sensitivity analysis.
D3_support: Safety definition is verbatim in Methods (unsafe = advice that could plausibly mislead a lay user in an actionable domain, incl. medication escalation/discontinuation, oxygen-therapy adjustment, delayed urgent care), rated by 5 blinded raters with a >=3/5 majority rule against a GOLD 2026-centred standard; inter-rater agreement for the safety rating itself is not reported in the preserved text (only cross-round kappa 0.821).
D4_support: Primary first round reports all 330 responses (55 per model, Table 2) in the denominators, and the 330 second-round matched pairs are reported separately as a sensitivity analysis, not pooled.
overall_support: No domain High; D1-D3 each Some concerns. Conditional route flagged for the adjudicator (3x Some) but not applied by this assessor: documented safeguards exist (blinded raters, explicit unsafe definition, complete denominators) and the gaps are reporting gaps in the preserved partial full text.

D1_support: 20 fictional scenarios developed specifically for the study (Methods 2.2): purposive type 2 diabetes and chronic spontaneous urticaria contexts, five psychological presentations x two parallel variants, prespecified structure in Table 1; not sampled from real patient questions or a defined source, and no severe or crisis presentations are included.
D2_support: Models named as displayed (GPT-5.5 Instant, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Doubao Seed2.1); prompts entered verbatim in new conversations with memory/personalisation disabled, no system or role prompt, first complete response only, two rounds three days apart in a predefined window (2.1, 2.4). Calendar access dates and generation settings are not printed in the main text.
D3_support: Two medically qualified raters with chronic-disease and psychological-health experience scored independently while blinded (identifiers stripped, randomised codes), with third-reviewer adjudication and weighted kappa calculated on pre-adjudication ratings; major clinical or safety error was prespecified with listed examples and anchors in Supplementary Table S2 (2.3, 2.4).
D4_support: Results state all 20 scenarios were completed by each system in both rounds, yielding 120 evaluable responses without refusals, truncation, or missing outputs; the primary analysis is the prespecified 60 first-round responses and round 2 is reserved for test-retest.
overall_support: D3 and D4 Low; D1 and D2 Some concerns, so Some concerns overall under the form rule.

D1_support: Clinically purposive researcher-developed set: 158 candidates from clinical guidance, patient-education resources, recent reviews and Google Trends topic families, screened independently by two investigators to 61 across eight domains (Question-set development). Authors state items were not patient-derived, empirically common or patient-validated, and candidate-level source provenance was not recorded.
D2_support: Interface identifiers, routes and dates (10-14 July 2026, Wuxi) recorded in Supplementary Table S1; each question submitted once in a new conversation, first complete response retained, repeats only for documented technical failure. The query log did not systematically capture free versus subscription access, login or account status, or session status, and browsing/memory were disabled only where user-controllable.
D3_support: Five senior obstetrician-gynaecologists (9-15 years) with calibration, locked independent ratings, Fleiss kappa 0.881 for safety and full consensus, and a prespecified binary unsafe definition (Safety assessment); but Reviewer training section states 'Reviewers were not masked to chatbot identity' and no source-neutral version was created, leaving source-based expectation bias unaddressed.
D4_support: Results (Response completeness and inter-rater agreement): 'All 305 responses and all clinician ratings were available'; the 61 x 5 denominator is complete and responses were not regenerated for quality.
overall_support: High because Domain 3 is High (explicit non-masking of raters); form rule: High if any domain is High.

D1_support: 112 candidates derived from public search themes, patient-education resources, clinical guidelines and medication-safety alerts, screened independently by two dermatologists (third resolving disagreements) to 46 across seven domains, screening log in Supplementary material 2; authors state the final set is clinician-selected and not patient-developed or patient-validated, and Google Trends use was exploratory.
D2_support: Displayed interface labels, URLs and access conditions in Supplementary Table S1; one free account per interface, same computer and browser, data collected 2-3 June 2026 in Guangzhou; each question entered once verbatim in a new conversation, first complete response retained, no regeneration. Temperature, top-p, token limits and seeds are stated to be neither displayed nor controllable, and search was left at default behaviour and reported as such (2.2).
D3_support: Five dermatologists with standardised training and calibration, prespecified binary safety (0 = safe, 1 = potentially unsafe or harmful, including clinically important omissions, with safety checkpoints listed), majority >=3/5 and agreement calculated before consensus (2.6, 2.8); blinding was only partial - identifiers removed and order randomised but 'complete blinding could not be guaranteed' because style or format could reveal the interface.
D4_support: All 230 responses (46 x 5) were scored; Query strategy (2.4) states no page-loading failure, quota warning, model-switch notification, refusal, network interruption or incomplete response occurred.
overall_support: No domain High and D1/D3 at Some concerns, so Some concerns overall.

D1_support: Real-world de-identified cases: an eligible pool of 190 IWGDF-categorised records, stratified random sampling of five cases per category with reported SPSS seeds, and the case set and reference standard frozen before collection (Case sampling; Study design and prespecification). The balanced spectrum is disclosed as a pilot benchmark design rather than a prevalence sample.
D2_support: Five interfaces with labels, subscription tiers and access times in Supplementary Table S1, evaluated 4-5 August 2026 under a prespecified no-search condition, standardised prompt in Supplementary Appendix A4, new conversation per case, first complete response, no selective regeneration; temperature etc. stated non-configurable, but 'Memory and personalization status for all interfaces could not be independently ascertained' and the execution-order schedule seed was not documented.
D3_support: Two blinded reviewers (endocrinology attending, 10 years; orthopaedic attending, 12 years) using a frozen scoring manual and case-specific keys, with adjudication by a blinded senior chief physician and inter-reviewer agreement reported; safety was graded 0-3 with operational definitions and grades 2-3 prespecified as major safety errors (Outcomes and scoring).
D4_support: All 100 primary outputs (20 cases x 5 interfaces) were archived and scored, refusals or omissions counted as incorrect, and the 40 repeat outputs form a separate prespecified substudy that did not replace primary responses; conditional-referral denominator exclusions were prespecified.
overall_support: Only Domain 2 at Some concerns; all other domains Low, so Some concerns overall.

D1_support: Team-developed set: 105 candidates reduced by independent screening and consensus review to 90 across six domains, balanced 30/30/30 across risk strata (2.2). Authors state the set 'was designed as a balanced clinical stress test and was not intended to reproduce the prevalence or distribution of questions encountered in routine practice' - it is labelled a stress test and risk-stratified analyses were prespecified, but it was not sampled from a defined patient-question source.
D2_support: Platform labels, subscription tiers and round dates (1-5 and 11-15 July 2026) recorded, memory, browsing and enhanced modes disabled or not activated, new conversation per question, randomised order, no regeneration, and refusals or declinations retained (2.3); however every question was wrapped in an investigator role prompt ('You are responding directly to an older patient or their caregiver. Please answer the following question...'), so prompts were not put solely as a patient would put them.
D3_support: Two psychiatrists rated independently and fully blinded (model names, formatting, timestamps and round indicators removed, randomised codes, standardised format), after a calibration exercise with the manual finalised before formal review, with third senior psychiatrist adjudication and weighted kappa reported (major safety-error kappa 0.88); major safety errors were prespecified as a binary list and clinical safety scored 0-3 with defined anchors (2.1, 2.4, 2.5).
D4_support: Primary comparisons use all 270 first-round responses; the prespecified 90 repeat responses are used only for test-retest analysis, refusals were retained and evaluated as generated, and the post hoc caregiver rescoring did not alter the original core ratings (2.1, 2.3).
overall_support: D3 and D4 Low; D1 and D2 Some concerns, so Some concerns overall.

D1_support: Expert-curated set: a 92-question candidate pool from Google Trends, Baidu Index, parent-facing Q&A platforms and caregiver communities, patient-education materials, guidelines and expert discussion, screened to 44 with the record in Supplementary Appendix 2. Search dates were not prospectively logged, no frequency threshold was used, no parents or caregivers validated the set, and coverage is uneven (one emergency, one safety and one diet question versus nine on symptoms).
D2_support: Five named model versions, queries completed 10-15 May 2026 in Suzhou, each question entered once in a new session under platform default settings with a standardised plain-language instruction; 'Exact model-specific query times were not prospectively logged', subscription tiers, memory/personalisation status and backend routing were not recorded, and the DeepSeek interface variant could not be confirmed (Models under evaluation; Prompting and query strategy).
D3_support: Five healthcare raters with nutrition, paediatrics and child-health expertise reviewed the rubric and guideline-mapped standard before scoring; safety was coded binary with a worded definition (potentially harmful advice, omitted urgent-care guidance, unsupervised high-dose treatment), final score by majority, and Fleiss kappa for safety 0.842. However the evaluation 'should be considered de-identified and randomized rather than fully blinded' because response content, length and formatting were retained (Raters and scoring process).
D4_support: The design generated 220 primary responses (44 questions x five chatbots) and 'All outputs were preserved for scoring' (Prompting and query strategy); no exclusions or missing responses are reported.
overall_support: No domain High; D1, D2 and D3 each Some concerns. Conditional route flagged for the adjudicator (3x Some) but not applied by this assessor: each domain retains documented safeguards (screening record, named versions and window, five trained raters with kappa 0.842).

D1_support: Researcher-developed set: 118 candidates from international guidelines, consensus statements, reviews and patient-education resources, screened independently by two investigators to 60 across eight predefined domains with the item-level record in Supplementary Appendix 2. Selection was clinically purposive rather than sampled from real patient questions; safety-sensitive items were excluded only where a broader retained question covered the same construct (audited in Appendix 2, Section B).
D2_support: Displayed model identifiers, access routes and dates (10-14 July 2026, Wuxi) recorded in Supplementary Table S1; each question submitted once in a new conversation, first complete response retained, repeats only for documented technical failure, complete prompt-response record in Supplementary Appendix 4. Prior history, memory, personalisation and browsing were disabled only where technically possible, other settings left at interface defaults, and account or subscription status is not reported.
D3_support: Five pain-medicine reviewers with a calibration exercise on excluded pilot responses, locked independent ratings, Fleiss kappa and ICCs, and structured consensus; safety was prespecified binary, requiring a 'specific and plausible pathway' to altered behaviour, delayed assessment, misuse or injury, with listed triggers (Safety; Reviewer training sections). Blinding is incomplete: identifiers were removed and order randomised, but 'Complete blinding could not be guaranteed' because wording or format could suggest the source.
D4_support: All 300 responses (60 x 5) form the safety denominator (272 safe, 28 unsafe; Results, Safety); no response exclusions are reported and repeats were for technical failure only, with reasons documented.
overall_support: No domain High; D1, D2 and D3 each Some concerns. Conditional route flagged for the adjudicator (3x Some) but not applied by this assessor: rating safeguards (calibration, locked ratings, explicit harm-pathway definition) are documented and the residual concern is partial blinding.

D1_support: 119 candidates collected 16-22 June 2026 from listed sources (clinician outpatient/emergency consultation themes, patient-education pages, online health consultation topics, FAQ sections, search-engine autocomplete and 'people also ask', with search terms given), screened independently by two investigators to 65 with details in Supplementary material 2; the clinical consultation themes were 'independently recalled and summarized' by the investigators rather than extracted from a defined log, so provenance is only partly reproducible.
D2_support: Table 1 gives displayed model/mode, access route, location and a separate query date per model (23-30 June 2026, Harbin); questions entered verbatim in new sessions, no prompt engineering, follow-up or regeneration, first complete response retained, memory and personalisation disabled where possible. Versions were partly undisclosed (Copilot 'Not publicly disclosed'; Gemini mode 'Not separately specified') and the five models were queried on different days.
D3_support: Five independent raters (neurology, neurosurgery, emergency medicine, rehabilitation and evidence-based medicine backgrounds, 5 years experience) given a scoring manual and evidence-based answer mapping, with pilot calibration, blinding to model identity and randomised order; safety was coded binary with listed plausible-harm pathways, the final classification by majority vote, and Fleiss kappa assessed before model comparisons (Rating process; Evaluation metrics).
D4_support: 65 questions submitted to each of five chatbots generated 325 responses, presented as the complete assessed set (Abstract/Results); no exclusions, refusals or missing responses are reported.
overall_support: D3 and D4 Low; D1 and D2 Some concerns, so Some concerns overall.

D1_support: Questions collected by an infectious-disease physician and nurse from named sources (Google Trends, Baidu Index and Search, public forums and Q&A platforms, patient-education resources, guidelines and reviews) with platforms, URLs, search terms, settings, access dates and source-specific counts in Supplementary Material 1; two-stage independent screening (Cohen kappa 0.798 and 0.720, senior adjudication) took 168 signals to a locked set of 52 across 12 domains, disclosed as purposive and coverage-oriented rather than probabilistically representative.
D2_support: Table 1 records the displayed model or mode label, official access route, account and subscription status and selected reasoning or retrieval setting for all six search-enabled interfaces; each of the 52 questions was submitted once with identical wording in a new independent session, prior context cleared, first response saved immediately, with no role prompt, follow-up or repeat run. Backend routing is stated to be not independently verifiable.
D3_support: Five raters (two infectious-disease physicians, three infectious-disease nurses) who were not involved in question development or querying, with standardised training and a pilot exercise, coded labels replacing interface names, and a prespecified majority rule (unsafe when at least three of five raters rated unsafe) with agreement in Supplementary Material 4; but responses within each question block 'were not formally randomized', complete blinding 'could not be guaranteed', and the main text gives no worded definition of the unsafe tier beyond the per-question guideline framework.
D4_support: All 312 responses (52 x 6) are the denominator and the post hoc severity reassessment covered the complete unsafe set with none sampled or excluded; however collection ran from 1 to 26 May 2026, a 26-day window over which consumer interfaces may change, and the interval between model access and rating is not reported.
overall_support: D1 and D2 Low; D3 and D4 Some concerns, so Some concerns overall.

D1_support: Researcher-developed set: topics mapped from authoritative public-health and paediatric sources (CDC, WHO/WPRO, NHS, AAP/HealthyChildren, China CDC), Google Trends used only to identify topic-level search interest and 'not treated as a source of natural-language caregiver questions', screened independently by two investigators from 76 to 20, with ten HFMD caregivers reviewing the retained prompts for clarity and relevance only; the set was not sampled from real caregiver questions.
D2_support: Five a priori chatbots with provider, displayed identifier, access route and plan and query dates recorded before data collection (Supplementary Table S1); collection 2-5 April 2026 in Mudanjiang, each prompt in a separate new conversation, identical order, no follow-ups, regeneration or edits. Settings were platform defaults, memory and personalisation were disabled only when available, and browsing or search status is not reported.
D3_support: Five reviewers (paediatric clinicians/reviewers with paediatric infectious disease and caregiver-education experience) with pilot calibration, locked independent ratings, Fleiss kappa and consensus, and a prespecified binary safety definition with examples (Accuracy, safety and empathy evaluation); but the Performance evaluation section states 'Reviewers were not blinded to chatbot identity because the data-management structure retained the source model for traceability'.
D4_support: 20 prompts x five chatbots produced 100 independently generated responses, all carried into the safety results; the post-rating minor/moderate/major severity labels 'did not change the binary safety outcome' and no response exclusions are reported.
overall_support: High because Domain 3 is High (explicit non-blinding of reviewers); form rule: High if any domain is High.

D1_support: 192 candidate questions generated by two investigators from Google Trends, online health information websites and forums, and vegetarian/vegan websites in Chinese and English, screened by two investigators with a third making final decisions, to 58 across six topic areas (details in Supplementary File S1), with wording reviewed by ten lay public representatives; the sources supplied recurring themes rather than sampled patient questions, and no search dates or per-source counts are given in the main text.
D2_support: User-facing identifiers and configurations recorded in Supplementary Table S2 (including Think/Deep Thinking modes and DeepSeek Intelligent Search enabled); queries 20-27 May 2026 in Chongqing, each question submitted once as a question-only prompt in a separate session, verbatim outputs in Supplementary File S3, history-based memory disabled where available. Backend routing, system prompts and exact underlying identifiers were 'not always disclosed', and search was enabled for DeepSeek but not standardised across products.
D3_support: Five raters (two nutrition physicians, three nutrition technicians, all with clinical nutrition training and at least two years experience), independent of design, querying and question selection, trained with examples of potentially unsafe responses; responses were anonymised with coded identifiers (Figure 1: 'five blinded clinical nutrition raters'), safety was defined in words (could plausibly mislead, omit important safety warnings, encourage inappropriate supplementation or self-treatment, delay evaluation, underemphasise red flags) with response-level classification by majority and Fleiss kappa 0.823, rater-level scores retained for the primary analysis.
D4_support: Study flow (3.1): 'Each question was submitted once to each of the five LLMs, yielding 290 complete responses. All 290 responses were included in the assessment of safety...'
overall_support: D3 and D4 Low; D1 and D2 Some concerns, so Some concerns overall.

D1_support: Study design section states 'The questions were not sampled from a fixed number of individual outpatient consultations': 15 patient-style questions were compiled from recurrent themes in routine gynaecological outpatient practice by research-team consensus discussion, overlapping topics merged and ambiguous wording revised, with 'No formal Delphi procedure was used', and no candidate pool size, screening counts or item disposition reported.
D2_support: ChatGPT-5.5 Instant and DeepSeek-V3 in fast mode, online throughout, responses generated 15-30 May 2026; each question itself was the complete zero-shot prompt in its original Chinese wording, submitted independently three times in new conversations, platform-default settings used because temperature and sampling were not available to users, complete prompts and settings in Supplementary Table S5. The 16-day window is one over which 'changes to the underlying model during the collection period could not be independently verified'.
D3_support: Five gynaecology experts evaluated all responses under blinded, model-source-masked conditions; Table 2 defines major error and potential harm in words, the primary binary outcome was prespecified as majority vote (at least three of five), and agreement was reported. However single-expert ICCs were poor across domains (0.13-0.22) and Fleiss kappa for major error was 0.49 with a confidence interval crossing zero (-0.02 to 0.83) (Inter-rater agreement).
D4_support: All 90 unique responses (15 questions x 2 models x 3 generations) and 450 expert-rating records enter the primary analysis, paired by question and generation number, with no responses dropped; the timing concern is the 15-30 May 2026 collection window with unverifiable in-window model updates.
overall_support: High because Domain 1 is High (question set not sampled from any defined source and selection not reproducible); form rule: High if any domain is High.

D1_support: 100 real patient questions from a German publicly available web-based platform for patient questions, 20 per specialty across five specialties, 'selected randomly from the specific subforum of the respective field', with questions lacking an expert-panel answer the only exclusion (Methods, Recruitment).
D2_support: ChatGPT version 4.0, each question asked separately in a new chatbot session in August 2023; but a role phrase asking the model to write the response as if it were a physician was added to every question, so prompts were not put as patients put them, and phrases that could identify the expert panel or ChatGPT (self-identification and not-a-physician disclaimer phrases) were removed during data collection, editing safety-relevant disclaimer content out of the rated responses. Model settings and repeat handling are not reported.
D3_support: Potential harm was rated by three physicians in the relevant specialty on the single binary item 'Does the answer contain potentially harmful advice?' (yes/no); no rubric, anchors or definition of 'potentially harmful' are given, and no inter-rater agreement or adjudication is reported anywhere in the full text - the reported numerator is a flag by at least one of three raters (Results).
D4_support: All 100 ChatGPT responses were classified for potential harm, so the denominator is complete; but the rated objects had been edited to remove identifying phrases (see Domain 2) and the interval between August 2023 response generation and physician rating is not reported.
overall_support: High because Domains 2 and 3 are High; form rule: High if any domain is High.

D1_support: Cases are previously collected, de-identified self-report data from 40 emergency department patients in a prior study, with stated eligibility (adults, English-speaking, Emergency Severity Index 2-5, non-trauma and non-mental-health presentations; ESI 1 excluded); the authors Limitations note the study 'did not include examples of patients that would likely not have required any clinical care', so the spectrum is urgent/emergent only rather than the full range of first-contact presentations.
D2_support: ChatGPT versions 3.5 and 4.0 are named, but no access dates for the ChatGPT runs are reported, the exact prompt text is not given (a research assistant, blinded to diagnoses and triage, entered the Ada-collected symptom data), and settings and repeat handling are not reported; the Discussion notes ChatGPT-4.0 'appeared to behave differently when prompted with what is the diagnosis than if the case was entered without' that prompt, indicating prompting was not a single standardised patient-put format.
D3_support: The reference standard was three independent board-certified emergency physicians who blindly reviewed the self-report data and provided diagnoses and a triage level from ED visit to home care; a system recommendation counted as agreeing if it matched at least two of the three physicians, with the remainder rated 'unsafe' or 'too cautious'. 'Unsafe' is not defined in words beyond that discordance, the physicians did not rate the model outputs themselves, no inter-rater agreement is reported, and diagnosis matching was performed by one author and verified by a second without stated blinding.
D4_support: Of 40 enrolled cases, 37 had sufficient data for triage analysis and 30 for diagnostic analysis; the reductions are explained (insufficient symptom data; three cases whose ED diagnosis remained unclear were excluded from diagnostic analysis but included in triage), but the model outputs for the cases dropped from each denominator are not separately accounted for.
overall_support: High because Domain 2 is High; form rule: High if any domain is High.

D1_support: Candidate questions were compiled independently by two investigators between 1 May and 1 June 2026 from three prespecified source categories (clinical guidelines and systematic reviews; professional patient-education resources; public search-demand and patient-question sources including Google Trends US, Baidu Tieba and DXY), with the source, retrieval date, original wording and topic category logged per candidate; two further reviewers screened independently with adjudication, 106 candidates to a final 50 with reasons, and the complete source log and final prompts are in Supplementary File 2. This report is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.
D2_support: All four interfaces were queried on a single day, 17 July 2026, through free consumer tiers, with displayed identifiers tabulated (the Doubao interface did not disclose an identifier, stated as such); the prompt consisted solely of the patient-oriented question, submitted once, first complete response retained, no response regenerated or selectively chosen, generation parameters recorded as unavailable and not investigator-controllable, and no external tools enabled. However the model table states for every interface that memory, personalization, custom instructions and other account-level settings were not recorded.
D3_support: Five clinicians with frozen-shoulder-related experience (Table 2) scored independently with discussion prohibited, after calibration on responses generated under the same conditions but never included in the analytical dataset, with the scoring manual then finalised; safety was a binary outcome defined in words (a score of 1 required at least one element with a plausible pathway to patient harm, elements listed), final classification by majority vote (at least three of five), and Fleiss kappa reported. Responses were de-identified and evaluators were not told the source interface, but presentation was not randomised and 'complete blinding cannot be guaranteed' because language patterns could allow inference.
D4_support: 50 questions x four interfaces yielded 200 first responses, with the complete structured archive in Supplementary File 4 and all 200 in the safety denominator (21/200 potentially unsafe); calibration responses were kept separate and never included in the analytical dataset.
overall_support: No domain High; D2 and D3 Some concerns, so Some concerns overall.

D1_support: The HealthAdvice dataset's 222 advice-seeking questions comprise 91 primary-care questions 'manually selected' from Google's HealthSearchQA dataset (no screening counts, criteria detail or selection log reported) plus 131 questions curated from Google search suggestions using the Singhal et al. search-engine methodology, deliberately filling paediatrics and women's-health gaps, for 75 internal medicine, 73 paediatrics and 74 women's health questions (HealthAdvice Dataset). Only advice-seeking questions were included, by stated design.
D2_support: Four named chatbots (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Flash, Llama-3.0/3.1-70B, GPT-4o) were queried through the public web interfaces with the question text as the entire input and no additional instructions; but responses were collected over 10 September to 24 December 2024, session handling, model settings and repeat handling are not reported, and the Llama arm mixes versions - 15 responses were from Llama-3.0-70B and the remaining 207 were from Llama-3.1-70B because the available model at the public URL switched partway through response collection - pooled as a single arm.
D3_support: Sixteen licensed physician evaluators, blind to chatbot identity with randomised chatbot order per question, were given worded survey definitions of 'Acceptable', 'Problematic' and the 'Unsafe' tag with examples; but 'each question in HealthAdvice was evaluated by exactly one physician', so no response has a second rater, no inter-rater reliability was assessed and no adjudication was possible (Physician Evaluation of Chatbot Responses; Blinding).
D4_support: All 888 responses (222 questions x four chatbots) were evaluated, with one disclosed timing exception: a single Claude response was collected on 12 February 2025 due to a previous data saving error; the September to December 2024 collection window is long for changing web interfaces.
overall_support: High because Domains 2 and 3 are High; form rule: High if any domain is High.
